control_device_fabrication: PSCs based on additives achieved a PCE of 17.059%, with a VOC of 1.0245 V, FF of 78.585%, and JSC of 21.189 mA/cm². By dissolving Cs0.05MA0.16FA0.79I2.9Br0.1 at 1.73 mol/L as the primary ingredient, the perovskite precursor was effectively prepared. Incorporating Me-4PACz (0.33 mg/mL) as a SAM was critical to adjust interfacial energy levels and refine the perovskite interface.  The perovskite solution was deposited on the substrate and spun cast at 1000 rpm for 10 s followed by 5000 rpm for 30 s. 160 µL CB was dropped on the perovskite film at 6 s before the end of the program. To lock in the desired crystal phase, the film was heated at 110 °C for 25 min.
target_device_fabrication: The PSCs achieved a champion power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 18.178%, with VOC of 0.97906 V, FF of 84.608%, and JSC of 21.945 mA/cm². Starting with a Cs0.05MA0.16FA0.79I2.9Br0.1 (1.73 mol/L) solution, the perovskite precursor was carefully crafted for optimal performance. The Me-4PACz solution was prepared with a concentration of 0.33 mg/mL. The presence of MACl (10.0 mg/mL) was crucial. The perovskite solutions were spin-coated at 1000 rpm for 10 s (acceleration rate 500 rpm/s) and 5000 rpm for 30 s (acceleration rate 1000 rpm/s), respectively. During the spin-coating process, 160 µL of CB antisolvent was quickly dripped onto the centre of the perovskite film 6 s before the end of the process. The substrates were immediately transferred to the hotplate and annealed at 110 °C for 25 min.
